name: Bubonic plague (flea- and louse-borne, as in the Second Pandemic)

reproduction_number_range.source: No source found: the Dean et al. 2018 PNAS abstract (doi 10.1073/pnas.1715640115, via Europe PMC) fits a human-ectoparasite model to nine European outbreaks but states no reproduction number, and the full text was not reachable (403); the range is kept as a labelled stand-in

transmissibility_per_day.source: A reproduction number of 1.4 divided by the infectious days

case_fatality.source: WHO plague fact sheet, who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/plague: 'a case-fatality ratio of 30% to 60% for the bubonic type'; 0.45 is the midpoint (the page gives no untreated qualifier for that range)

immunity.source: No source found: the WHO plague fact sheet makes no statement on immunity; lifelong immunity is a labelled assumption

stage.incubating.source: WHO plague fact sheet: 'an incubation period of one to seven days'; the 4 day mean is the midpoint. Shape 4 is a middling spread, not sourced

stage.infectious.source: No source found for the length of the infectious stage; kept as a labelled stand-in. Shape 2 is a broad spread, not sourced

density_exponent.source: Heuristic inside the range Rader et al. 2020 supports (crowded cities see longer epidemics with larger attack rates; weaker than linear); vary across the ensemble
